issues.description: Stock#getStockIngredients() has incompatible return types between starter code and reference solution. In the template, getStockIngredients() returns List<StockIngredient> (wrapping the internal array via Arrays.asList), but in the solution it returns StockIngredient[]. Students following the template API will write List-based code, while tests/solution expect an array-based accessor, causing compilation/type errors and confusion about the intended public API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the starter template with the intended array-based API: change template Stock#getStockIngredients() to return StockIngredient[] (and remove the Arrays.asList/List return), matching the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting guidance about whether SealSaloon methods/field are static: the UML diagram lists SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) without any static marker, but later the text explicitly requires stock, acceptSupplyDelivery, and calculateTotalPrice to be static (and the solution implements them as static). This inconsistency can lead students to implement instance methods when the tests/solution expect static members.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML in problem_statement.md to explicitly mark static members (e.g., {static} or underlining) for stock, acceptSupplyDelivery, and calculateTotalPrice so the diagram matches the textual requirement and solution.

issues.description: SealSaloon#getStock() is used as an instance method in the provided Main example (shop.getStock()), but the reference solution declares getStock() as static. This inconsistency can cause confusion about how students should access the (required) static stock and may lead to compilation differences depending on which style they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Make usage consistent with the intended static stock: either update Main/example code to call SealSaloon.getStock() statically, or additionally provide an instance method getStock() that delegates to the static field while keeping the field itself static.
